![documentation · low](https://img.shields.io/badge/documentation-low-green) PP10: The comment is stale/inaccurate: `makeBatchManager`'s parameter is passed by value and it silently falls back to the synchronous backend, so the parameter is not a mere "preference" that "has no further effect" after a failed io_uring setup — the effective backend (io_uring vs. synchronous) is a user-visible observable behavior of the parameter (see src/index/vocabulary/VocabularyOnDisk.cpp:512-516, where it is read once at `open`). Please reword to state precisely that setting it to `false` forces the synchronous backend, and that a fallback may still occur if io_uring is unavailable. It does not state that sizes are obtained via `ql::ranges::size` (so all arguments must be sized ranges), what happens when `rest` is empty (the fold is vacuously `true`, so a single-argument call always succeeds silently), or which exception type is thrown. ![documentation · low](https://img.shields.io/badge/documentation-low-green) PP10: The comment above the `detail` namespace says `makeBatchManagerFor` (the helper added at the bottom of this file) defines the test hook declared in `PageCacheFirstPolicy.h`, and that production code only goes through `readPageCacheHits`. Neither is true anymore: the hook is `PageCacheRead`/`pageCacheRead`, declared in `src/util/PageCacheReadHook.h`, and `makeBatchManager` calls `detail::makeBatchManagerFor` directly. Please correct or drop this comment.
